calls.summary: Patricia Nguyen called to find a doctor for ongoing chest tightness and wanted a cardiology evaluation. Agent Rosey used Find a Doctor to match her with a Heart and Vascular specialist and booked a new patient consultation at the Dallas campus. Patricia confirmed her insurance and left satisfied.

Marcus Bell called seeking a second opinion in oncology after a recent diagnosis at another hospital. Agent Lila explained the intake process at Simmons Comprehensive Cancer Center and scheduled a new consultation with a medical oncologist. Marcus was relieved to get cancer care access within the week.

Diane Foster called to schedule an MRI that her referring physician had ordered for a knee injury. Agent Lee verified the order, found an open slot at the imaging center, and booked the MRI study for the following Tuesday. Diane appreciated the quick turnaround.

Ronald Simmons, a new patient relocating to Dallas, called to establish primary and preventive care. Agent Mary collected his demographics, insurance details, and medical history, then scheduled a new patient wellness visit at the North Dallas location. Ronald confirmed the appointment and requested a MyChart activation code.

Elena Vasquez called to find a doctor for chronic hip pain and hoped for an orthopaedic surgery evaluation. Agent Mike reviewed her symptoms, explained the joint replacement consultation process, and scheduled a new patient appointment. Elena was pleased with the same-week option.

Gregory Lin called because he could not log into MyChart to view his lab results. Agent Sue verified his identity and walked him through resetting his MyChart password. The issue was resolved on the call, and no visit was needed.

Sandra Okafor called to move up her oncology follow-up after new symptoms appeared. Agent Jennifer coordinated with the care team and scheduled an earlier appointment with her medical oncologist. Sandra thanked the agent for the flexibility.

Thomas Reilly called disputing a billing statement he felt was higher than the estimate he received. Agent Oscar reviewed the charges and opened a billing review case, but could not resolve the amount on the call. Thomas remained frustrated and asked for a callback.

Karen Mitchell called with questions about the results from a recent MRI that had not yet appeared in her portal. Agent Rose explained that the radiologist read was still pending and that her physician would follow up. Karen was anxious about the delay.

David Huang called to cancel an upcoming neurology appointment because of a scheduling conflict at work. Agent Lila processed the cancellation and offered to rebook later, but David declined for now. He said he would call back next month.

Angela Barnes called because her MyChart account was locked after several failed login attempts. Agent Lee attempted to reset it but the system required an in-person verification step. Angela was annoyed at the extra hurdle.

Robert Nash called with a billing complaint about a duplicate charge on his imaging visit. Agent Mike documented the concern and escalated it to the billing department for investigation. Robert was upset that it could take up to ten business days.

Linda Carver called to complain about wait times during her cancer treatment infusion visits at the center. Agent Sue apologized and logged the feedback for the clinical team, but could not offer an immediate fix. Linda ended the call still dissatisfied.

James Whitfield called after hours trying to reschedule a transplant evaluation appointment. The call rolled to voicemail and no agent was available to assist. He left a message requesting a callback the next morning.

Michelle Torres called angry that her referral had not been processed and she still could not book a specialist. Agent Oscar tried to locate the referral but the record was incomplete on the call. Michelle was frustrated and threatened to seek care elsewhere.

prompts.question: Is the patient trying to solve a specific problem?
prompts.answer: Yes. The caller (prospective new patient) is experiencing left shoulder pain and mobility restriction. She is seeking evaluation and treatment options from an orthopedic surgeon at UT Southwestern and wants to book a consultation appointment to begin the diagnostic and care-planning process.

prompts.question: What are the patient's expectations?
prompts.answer: The patient expects to be seen by an orthopedic specialist, have a thorough examination, receive a diagnosis and treatment plan, and schedule the appointment within a reasonable timeframe (she accepted the offered date without hesitation). She is a new patient to UT Southwestern and is likely comparing this experience to other local providers.

prompts.question: How could the agent handle the call better?
prompts.answer: Marcus should have confirmed the patient's email address before closing (it was not captured), offered parking and transportation guidance (UT Southwestern's Dallas campus has valet and public options), and briefly explained the pre-visit paperwork and MyChart portal setup so the patient knows what to expect. These additions would reduce call-backs and no-shows.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling UT Southwestern Medical Center orthopedic appointments. This is Marcus speaking. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Marcus. Yes, I'm calling because I've had really bad left shoulder pain for about three weeks now and a friend recommended I see someone at UT Southwestern. I'm not sure if I need surgery or what, but I want to talk to a doctor about it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm glad you reached out to us. Left shoulder pain is definitely something our orthopedic team can evaluate. I'd like to get you scheduled with one of our specialists. Can I start by getting your full name, please?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Of course. It's Sarah Chen. C as in Charlie, H as in Hotel, E as in Echo, N as in November.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect, Sarah Chen. Thank you. And Sarah, are you a current UT Southwestern patient, or will this be your first visit with us?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: First time. I've never been to UT Southwestern before.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. I'll get you set up as a new patient. Do you have insurance coverage, Sarah, or are you planning to self pay?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: I have Blue Cross Blue Shield through my employer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great, that's helpful. And just to confirm, are you located in the Dallas area? What's your ZIP code?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, I'm in Dallas. It's 75204. That's close to the medical center, right?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, that's very close. Our main campus is right there. Now, I have an opening with one of our orthopedic surgeons next Tuesday, October 22 at 2 PM. Does that work for your schedule?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: October 22 at 2 PM works perfectly. I'll be there.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. So to confirm, Sarah Chen, new patient orthopedic consultation for left shoulder pain, next Tuesday October 22 at 2 PM here at UT Southwestern. You'll receive a confirmation email shortly with all the details. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: No, that sounds good. Thank you so much.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Sarah. Thank you for choosing UT Southwestern Medical Center, and we look forward to seeing you on the 22nd. Have a great day.

callDetail.aiSummary: Sarah Chen, a new patient in Dallas ZIP 75204 with Blue Cross Blue Shield insurance, called to schedule an orthopedic consultation for left shoulder pain persisting for three weeks. Marcus Bell completed the intake efficiently, capturing her name, insurance status, and location, and booked her for a new patient orthopedic appointment on Tuesday, October 22 at 2 PM at UT Southwestern's main campus. The call proceeded smoothly with clear confirmation of appointment details, though email address was not captured and patient expectations around pre-visit forms and parking were not addressed.

comment.author: Kyle Paklaian
comment.text: @Marcus, excellent structure and professional tone on this new patient orthopedic intake. You nailed the greeting, captured all required demographics, and booked the appointment with clear confirmation. Two quick coaching points for next time: (1) Always grab the email address before you close, so we can send confirmation and reduce no-shows. (2) Briefly mention that she'll receive pre-visit forms via MyChart and note our parking options at the campus. These small touches set expectations and reduce call-backs. Well done overall.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling UT Southwestern Medical Center, this is Diane. How can I help you today?
highlights: Thank you for calling UT Southwestern Medical Center

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi Diane. My name is Robert Alvarez, I'm a new patient. My wife was just diagnosed with breast cancer and we're looking for a second opinion at your Simmons cancer center.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I'm so sorry to hear that, Robert, and I'm glad you reached out. UT Southwestern's Harold C. Simmons Comprehensive Cancer Center is the only NCI-designated center in North Texas. Can I get her name and a callback number to start?
highlights: Harold C. Simmons Comprehensive Cancer Center

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Sure, it's Maria Alvarez, and the best number is 214-555-0148.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you. And do you have her pathology reports and imaging available? That helps our breast oncology team review her case before the visit.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: We have the biopsy report from the other hospital. Honestly we already started talking to Baylor down the road, but everyone keeps telling us to check with you first.
highlights: already started talking to Baylor down the road

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's a very common comparison, and I'd say the difference is our multidisciplinary tumor board and clinical trial access. Every case is reviewed by surgical, medical, and radiation oncology together. Would you like a new patient consultation with our breast oncology team?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Yes, but before we go further, what does a consult like that run? We're still sorting out what insurance covers and I want to keep this manageable.
highlights: what does a consult like that run

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Understandable. A new patient specialist consultation typically ranges from about $250 to $500 for self-pay, but most of it is billed through insurance. I can also connect you with a financial counselor who reviews assistance options before your first visit.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Okay, that helps. One more thing, she'll also need genetic testing at some point, is that something you handle there too?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Yes, we have a full cancer genetics program on site, so her oncologist can order that during the same care plan. No need to go anywhere else.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: That's good to hear. The tricky part is timing, her surgeon at the other place wants an answer within two weeks, so I'd need something soon.
highlights: wants an answer within two weeks

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: I can work with that. I have a new patient breast oncology consultation open this Thursday at 10 AM at our Simmons Cancer Center on Harry Hines. Shall I book that for Maria?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Let me just confirm with Maria quickly... yes, Thursday at 10 works for us. Please book it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Wonderful. You're scheduled for Thursday at 10 AM. I'll send a MyChart invite so you can upload her records ahead of time, and a financial counselor will call before the visit.
highlights: You're scheduled for Thursday at 10 AM

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Thank you, Diane. That's a big relief.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome, Robert. Take care, and we'll see Maria Thursday.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi this is Sarah from UT Southwestern. We received your inquiry about scheduling a cardiology consultation. Is this still a good time to chat?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yes hi. I need to see a heart specialist. My primary care doc recommended UT Southwestern.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great! We're glad your doctor referred you. To find the right cardiologist for you, are you looking for a diagnostic evaluation, or do you have a known heart condition you'd like us to manage?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: I have high blood pressure and my doctor thinks I might need further testing. Maybe an echo or something.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That makes sense. An echocardiogram is a great first step. Have you ever had heart imaging done before, or would this be your first time?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: First time. I'm pretty nervous about it honestly.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's completely normal. Our team will walk you through everything. Quick question, are you insured, or would you prefer to discuss self pay options?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: I have Blue Cross. So I'm covered.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. With your insurance, we can get you scheduled quickly. We have openings next week. Would Tuesday March 18th at 2 pm or Thursday March 20th at 10 am work better for you?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Tuesday the 18th at 2 pm is perfect.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Excellent. I'm booking you with Dr. Michael Chen in our Cardiology program at our main campus on Harry Hines Boulevard. Your appointment is Tuesday March 18th at 2 pm. We'll send you a text reminder the day before. Can you confirm the phone number we're using is 214-555-0847?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yes that's correct.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. If you have any questions before your visit, you can call us back at 214-645-8989. Thanks for choosing UT Southwestern, and we look forward to seeing you!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi there, thanks for calling UT Southwestern Medical Center. This is Marcus. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah, hi. I'm looking to get a second opinion on my cancer treatment. I heard you guys have a really good oncology program.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Absolutely. Our Simmons Comprehensive Cancer Center is ranked among the best in the nation. I'd be happy to help you schedule a consultation. Have you been treated elsewhere, or is this your first time seeking oncology care?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: No, I've already had some chemo at another facility. I just want to make sure I'm getting the best possible treatment plan.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That makes total sense. A second opinion is a great step. What type of cancer are you dealing with, if you don't mind me asking?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: It's stage two lung cancer. They said I might need radiation after the chemo, but I want to explore all my options.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Got it. Lung cancer, stage two. We have excellent outcomes with our multidisciplinary tumor board approach. We can have you in to see one of our oncologists. Are you looking to come in sometime this month, or do you prefer early next month?

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: I'm pretty flexible. Whatever's soonest would be best for me.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Perfect. How about Tuesday, January twenty-eighth at two o'clock in the afternoon? That would give you about two weeks to gather your prior records.

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Yeah, that works for me. What do I need to bring?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Great. Please bring your insurance card, a photo ID, and any prior imaging or treatment records you have. Your appointment is Tuesday, January twenty-eighth at two PM at our main campus on Harry Hines Boulevard in Dallas. Your confirmation number is seven four nine three two eight. If you need to reach us before then, just call eight seven seven, nine three six, twenty-nine thirty-three.

transcript.speaker: consumer
transcript.text: Perfect. Thanks so much. I really appreciate it.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome. We're looking forward to seeing you. Have a great day.

brandConversationRules: Intro and offer: Introduce yourself as UT Southwestern Medical Center's AI scheduling assistant here to help match the patient with the right specialist and secure a personalized appointment, mention that new patients can often be seen within a few days at our Dallas locations, and ask if they'd like to get started.

Qualify one question at a time: Ask a single question per message to learn the reason for the visit or condition, whether they are a new or returning patient, which specialty or provider they need, their preferred timeframe and location, and finally their ZIP code to confirm we serve their area.

Estimate then book: Confirm we care for patients in their ZIP code, share what a first visit and evaluation generally involves without quoting exact pricing since charges depend on insurance and services, recommend a consultation with the appropriate specialist for a full care plan, propose a specific day and time, and confirm they will receive a reminder text before the appointment with a number to call.

qaPairs.question: How do I find a doctor at UT Southwestern?
qaPairs.answer: You can search our Find a Doctor directory by specialty, condition, or provider name. Tell me what you need care for and I will help match you with the right specialist and book a visit.

qaPairs.question: Are you accepting new patients?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, most of our specialties and primary care clinics are accepting new patients across the Dallas area. Share the reason for your visit and I will get you scheduled with the appropriate provider.

qaPairs.question: Do you take my insurance?
qaPairs.answer: UT Southwestern participates with most major insurance plans, though coverage varies by plan and service. Our team can verify your benefits when we schedule your appointment, so let's find a time that works for you.

qaPairs.question: How soon can I be seen?
qaPairs.answer: Many new patients can be seen within a few days, and some specialties offer same-week visits. Tell me your preferred location and timeframe and I will find the earliest opening.

qaPairs.question: Where are your locations?
qaPairs.answer: We have hospitals and clinics throughout the Dallas-Fort Worth area, including our main campus and neighborhood locations. Let me know which area is convenient and I will book you nearby.

qaPairs.question: Can I get a second opinion on my cancer diagnosis?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our Simmons Comprehensive Cancer Center offers second-opinion consultations with our oncology specialists and tumor board. I can schedule an evaluation for you if you share a bit about your diagnosis.

qaPairs.question: Do I need a referral to be seen?
qaPairs.answer: Some specialties and insurance plans require a referral, while others allow you to book directly. Tell me the type of care you need and I will let you know and get you scheduled.

qaPairs.question: How much will my visit cost?
qaPairs.answer: Charges depend on your insurance, the specialist you see, and the services provided, so I cannot quote an exact price. The best next step is to book a consultation where our team can review your coverage and care plan.

qaPairs.question: Can I schedule an MRI or imaging study?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we offer high-field MRI, CT, and PET imaging with radiologist reads at several locations. I can help you book an imaging appointment once your provider has ordered the study.

qaPairs.question: How do I access MyChart?
qaPairs.answer: MyChart is our secure patient portal for messages, results, and appointment reminders, and you can sign up at our website or during your first visit. I can also help you schedule an appointment right now.

qaPairs.question: Do you offer virtual visits?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, many of our providers offer video visits in addition to in-person appointments. Let me know your preference and I will find an available time.

qaPairs.question: Can I see a heart specialist?
qaPairs.answer: Our Heart and Vascular Care team offers diagnostics, procedures, and surgical care with nationally ranked cardiologists. Share your symptoms or referral and I will book you with the right specialist.

qaPairs.question: I need orthopaedic care for my knee, who do I see?
qaPairs.answer: Our orthopaedic surgeons treat joint conditions from evaluation through surgery and rehab coordination. I can schedule a consultation to get your knee assessed and a care plan started.

qaPairs.question: Do you treat neurological conditions like stroke or epilepsy?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our Neurology and Neurosurgery teams provide multidisciplinary care for stroke, epilepsy, and brain and spine conditions. Tell me more about your needs and I will book you with the appropriate team.

qaPairs.question: Can I book a primary care or wellness visit?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, our primary and preventive care providers handle wellness exams, screenings, and chronic-disease management. Let me know your preferred location and I will find you an appointment.

qaPairs.question: How do I enroll in a clinical trial?
qaPairs.answer: UT Southwestern offers clinical trials that provide access to investigational therapies, typically at no cost to participants. I can help you schedule a consultation to discuss whether a trial is right for you.

qaPairs.question: What makes UT Southwestern different?
qaPairs.answer: We are the No. 1 hospital in DFW for the tenth year in a row with more nationally ranked specialties than any hospital in Texas. Let me help you book with one of our specialists to experience that care.

qaPairs.question: Can I request a specific doctor?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, if you have a preferred provider I can check their availability and book you directly. Just share the doctor's name and your preferred timeframe.

qaPairs.question: My symptoms are getting worse, what should I do?
qaPairs.answer: If this is an emergency please call 911 or go to the nearest emergency room right away. For urgent but non-emergency concerns, I can help you find the soonest available appointment with the right specialist.

qaPairs.question: Can I transfer my care to UT Southwestern?
qaPairs.answer: Yes, we welcome patients transferring their care and can coordinate records from your current provider. Let me know the type of care you need and I will schedule your first visit.
